source.display_title: 05/15/2026 - Brad Custis x Farooq Bey  — Lost

rep.name: Farooq Bey
rep.location: Medellín, Colombia (Nigerian ethnically, grew up in London)

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter call referenced. The prospect described a self-serve inbound path: "I saw a video on, think it was on YouTube... from Trevor, and then from him, and then from there, it was like, fill out this if you're interested."

prospect.name: Brad Custis
prospect.occupation: Agricultural products sales, and a pastor — holds both roles
prospect.training_background: Barbell training on a home squat rack since his teens, self-described as inconsistent. Pulled a hamstring around September 2025 and has done essentially nothing since except walking and some upper-body work — "I don't trust myself right now". Bought a dual set of 12kg kettlebells and has never used them.
prospect.medical: Two disclosures, neither followed up by the rep. (1) A hamstring injury roughly eight months earlier that still governs what he will attempt: "I had an injury probably six months ago... I've literally walked, all I've been doing is walking... I don't trust myself right now." (2) Raised blood sugar with a clinician-presented fork between lifestyle and medication: "right now I've taken like my blood, uh, you know, my sugars up... they're like, you either go the dietary route or you go the medicine route. And I'm like, I would rather do diet and exercise before I go down the medicine side." No clinician, clearance or current-treatment question was ever asked.

signals: Lost ground to an injury and a busy season and wants the former self back — 'I've been physically decently fit in the past, just with everything else I'm not right now'
Carries explicit regret about it: 'I'm pretty disciplined in many areas of my life, Farooq... the thing is like, why haven't I figured this out?'
The injury was the trigger: 'in my mind, I shouldn't, pulling a hamstring shouldn't make me this, like, it made everything more real'
Overlaps with the_preserver on the money dimension — nominally respectable income, four kids and a hard ceiling: 'I can't spend $6,000'

goals.text: Stay functional and mobile as he ages — able to hike, play and travel with kids and eventually grandkids
Build strength and flexibility at the same time rather than trading one for the other
Get body fat down by 10-15% and lose weight
Bring his blood sugar down through diet and exercise instead of starting medication
Become durable enough to trust his own body again after the hamstring injury
Have the physical side of his life match the spiritual discipline he already has — 'what I preach from the spiritual side also shows up on the physical side'
Train effectively inside a packed schedule without needing two-hour sessions
See early visible wins, like not being out of breath on the stairs

pains.text: Raised blood sugar and a live decision between the dietary route and starting medication
Hamstring injury around September that has kept him off lower-body training for roughly eight months
Lost trust in his own body — will not load it because he does not believe it will hold
Repeated problems with barbell training over the years
Bought kettlebells and never used them because he does not know what he is doing with them
Two jobs, four kids, no room for a two-hour workout
Has spoken to several coaches and not found the right fit — every one ends at a number he considers ridiculous
Disciplined everywhere else in life and cannot work out why this one area has never been solved

objections.raw_quote: People use the words, uh, business owner, uh, entrepreneur, busy things, because then all of a sudden, uh, it, here comes the hammer for some stupid, ridiculous number. Just being real straight. I've had a couple of people and it's like, so that's where, that's what, that's what, everything sounds great until we get to here.
objections.rep_response: Positioned rather than explored — 'we're not the most expensive. We're not the cheapest either. You know, so if you want to brace yourself, brace yourself' — then went straight to the numbers without addressing the objection he had just been handed

objections.raw_quote: It's just, I, I just too rich for my blood when it really comes down to it, man... I don't think I can do it... No, no, I know. I know I can't. I can't spend $6,000. I can't spend $6,000.
objections.rep_response: One half-probe — 'You don't think or?' — and on the flat answer the core offer was abandoned within seconds and replaced with a $200/month self-serve subscription. No isolation, no financial picture, none of the OC play

objections.raw_quote: No, just give me some time to chew on it, and I'm going to hold for right now, but I'll do a little more research on it, look into it, and then go from there.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and ended the call warmly; no OA play, no follow-up booked, no link sent

offer.payment_plan_terms: Credit card described as the usual route, plus 'in-house payment plan options if necessary', plus Klarna or 'Paver' spreading over 12 months 'at just a little bit of interest on top'. Nothing was structured — the prospect declined before any plan was worked out.

evidence: Unambiguous refusal, stated three times and confirmed when probed: 'I know I can't. I can't spend $6,000. I can't spend $6,000.'
The $200/month Primal University downsell was also not taken: 'just give me some time to chew on it, and I'm going to hold for right now'
No payment, no link, no follow-up call booked, no next contact agreed; the rep closed with 'Nice to meet you, Brad'

Counter-evidence, and the reason this is not a total loss: he was warm on the lower-priced product — 'I'll look into it on that primary university that makes sense because that's definitely probably more where I'm at and thinking for sure'
Counter-evidence on intent rather than money: high stated alignment throughout, and he apologised for taking the rep's time
outcome.next_step: Prospect to research Primal University ($200/month, cancel anytime) in his own time. Nothing scheduled and no follow-up owned by the rep.

notable.note: Two things a principal should see. First, the prospect disclosed raised blood sugar and a clinician-presented choice between diet and medication, and the rep's entire response was 'Okay. Okay. Okay. Yep, yep' — then later gave him a specific starting kettlebell weight. Second, when the $6,000 landed the rep ran none of the money play and instead downsold to a $200/month subscription, telling the prospect he could take one month, extract what he needed and cancel, prefaced with 'It's just between you and I'. The prospect also rejected the ICP framing to the rep's face: 'People use the words business owner, entrepreneur... I also have four kids. I have bills I have to pay. So it's not just successful and those type of things.'

quality.notes: Sustained mis-attribution on turn boundaries, with several full inversions. At 00:04:36-00:04:53 the question 'And since September, have you been working out?' is split across both labels; at 00:11:56-00:12:00 the rep's summary is labelled Brad Custis; at 00:13:00 'Now, on the kettlebell side, Brad, it's just really simple' is labelled Brad Custis but is obviously the rep; at 00:20:28-00:20:54 the rep's account of moving to Medellín is split so that 'That was nine months ago, yeah' lands under Brad Custis; at 00:22:22-00:22:43 the price statement itself straddles both labels. Roles were resolved from content throughout. No dropouts or truncation.
